doc.name: A — tea catalogue, floating levitation, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: loose-leaf tin with scoop
Category: tea
Shot programme: floating levitation
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the art director signing off every frame of this tea campaign. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the in-context lifestyle in a floating levitation treatment.

SUBJECT. A loose-leaf tin with scoop. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Product in its real use environment with lived-in supporting props. Shoot on a 135mm telephoto at f/11, framing for frame-within-frame using foreground architecture.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with north-facing window light with a black v-flat for negative fill. Stage the product on or against frosted glass, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a clean high-key grade with the whites pushed to the edge of clipping. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Emit one prompt, one paragraph, no framing text of any kind before or after it.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
